advances: A full-normal minimizing-cap formula at prescribed marks and a two-sided directional-transfer example. For long extrusions the prescribed mark is strictly shallower than an explicit actual competitor.

proof:
Convexity follows from the concave upper roof and constant lower roof. Fubini gives the total mixed area. For the indicated $h$, the slab over $X$ with heights $[2h-g(-X),g(X)]$ lies in $[-L,g(X)]$, since $2h-g(-X)\ge-L$. Its heights are ordered because $h\le\min_Dg$ gives $2h\le g(X)+g(-X)$. The resulting subset is symmetric about $(0,h)$, which belongs to the actual body since its integer base is zero and $-L\le h\le g(0)$. The subset's mixed mass is $2(Q-hW)$ by the lattice-preserving reflection $X\mapsto-X$. Every closed halfspace containing its center captures at least half its mass, since it contains at least one member of each reflected pair. The cap $t\ge h$ has area $Q-hW$ by Fubini, giving equality over all ambient halfspaces, including pure base directions.

The section at $0$ is precisely $D$. Its reflection gives raw section depth at least $W/2$ at the origin. The complementary closed section halfspaces $s\ge0$ and $s\le0$ have equal mass and a measure-zero common boundary, so they cover the section at the common budget $W/2$. As $g>0$ and $L>0$, all positive fibers are cut properly at $t=0$. The normalization at $(0,0)$ is $Q/(LW+Q)$. For $L>2Q/W$ the point $(0,-L/2)$ has raw depth at least $LW/2>Q$ by the contained symmetric cylinder $D\times[-L,0]$.

In the explicit example the complete base set is $-1,0,1$. Each section interval has length $2$ and each original fiber has area $17/2$. Integrating the affine roof on each interval gives area $5/2$ above the section and area $6$ below it. The roof extrema are $1/4$ and $9/4$, so the stated range is exactly the range of the sufficient conditions. In the direction $s\ge0$, the three half-intervals have total length $3$. Their positive mass is $3\int_0^1(5/4-s)\,ds=9/4$ and their lower mass is $9$, giving the two fractions.
statement:
Let $D\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R$ be a compact convex body centrally symmetric about $0$, with mixed length measure $\nu$ of mass $W>0$. Let $g$ be continuous, positive and concave on $D$, and let $L\ge\max_Dg$. Set $Q=\int_Dg\,d\nu$ and $C=\{(X,t):X\in D,\ -L\le t\le g(X)\}$. The total mixed area is $LW+Q$. Whenever $(\max_Dg-L)/2\le h\le\min_Dg$, the raw depth at the actual point $(0,h)$ is $Q-hW$, attained by $\{t\ge h\}$. The section $t=0$ is $D$ and has normalized maximum depth $1/2$. At $h=0$ the original cap cuts every positive fiber properly and the original normalized depth tends to zero as $L\to\infty$ with $D,g$ fixed.

For $D=[-1,1]\times[-1,1]$ in coordinates $(z,s)$, with $z$ integer, take $g=5/4-s$ and $L=3$. Then $W=6$, $Q=15/2$ and the total mixed area is $51/2$. On $-3/8\le h\le1/4$ the raw depth is $15/2-6h$, and the original normalized depth at $h=0$ is $5/17$. The direction $\{s\ge0\}$ captures half the section and half the lower area at $t=0$, but only $3/10$ of the upper cap's area.
title: Exact depth along a transverse interval in a reflected roof body
